entities.summary: Joseph Hueber (unknown-1787) was a pivotal Austrian baroque master builder who studied under Johann Lukas von Hildebrandt. Born in the early 18th century, Hueber rose to prominence through his collaboration with prominent architects and engineers of the time. His work, characterized by grandiose designs and innovative structural solutions, had a lasting impact on the development of European architecture. Hueber's legacy can be seen in the numerous buildings and landmarks he designed, including the iconic St. Stephen's Cathedral in Vienna. His contributions to the field of architecture not only showcased his skill as a master builder but also paved the way for future generations of architects. As a testament to his enduring influence, Hueber's work continues to inspire architects and historians alike.
